newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Unilever firm as profits delight.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Unilever firm as profits delight.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever Plc/NV announced on Friday an unexpected 24 percent leap in its half year profits to 1.374 billion pounds ($2.2 billion) sending its shares skyward.

The 24 percent increase, which excludes profits from the sale of its speciality chemicals business to Imperial Chemical Industries Plc for $8 billion in early July, exceeded all stock market forecasts.

Analysts expected profits before tax in the second quarter, excluding the sale of speciality chemicals, to fall between 730 and 780 million pounds compared with the actual 37 percent increase to 836 million.

Unilever Plc shares were 27 pence higher in London at 1796p, and in Amsterdam Unilever N.V. gained 9.10 guilders to 464.10. The company also announced a proposed share split in both the British and Dutch arms on a four-for-one basis.
For the six months to June 30, 1997 the group made pre-tax profit of 4.39 billion pounds including a 3.02 billion profit from the sale of its speciality chemicals division.
The sale propelled Unilever from debt into a net cash position at the half year of about 2.8 billion pounds ($4.6 billion).
Analysts were also impressed by the strong margin improvement, especially in Europe.

Margins in the region climbed 12 percent in the second quarter up from 9.5 percent over the same period last year while trading profits from the group's European businesses increased to 484 million pounds up from 385 million.
But comments by chairman Niall Fitzgerald, in a statement attached to the half year results, tempered any over enthusiasm.
He said profits growth in the remainder of the year would be less buoyant and sales growth is likely to remain modest.
"Although profits growth in the remainder of the year will be less buoyant, profit improvement for the full year will be satisfactory," said Fitzgerald.
He added that the group does not expect economic conditions to change much in the rest of the year.

Sterling's strength and the weakness of the guilder compared to last year is likely to have a significant impact on the group's full year results when expressed at current exchange rates, said Fitzgerald.
Chief press officer Mike Haines said in an interview this meant taking a hit of 50 million in the three months to June 30 and about 70 million in the year to date.
Analysts expressed some disappointment with the poor sales growth of one percent in the second quarter to 8.83 billion pounds and the weak outlook from the company.
"For the first time in a number of years the net effect of acquisitions less disposals has had a negative impact on sales and reduced sales growth by one percent," said Haines.
"However the underlying volume of continuing business, excluding speciality chemicals, grew by two percent," he added.

So far this year the group has sold its speciality chemicals business, the professional haircare business of Helene Curtis, maple syrup firm Mrs Butterworth and its Nordsee fish restaurant, wholesale and retail business and John West Foods.
"In our developing and emerging markets sales increased buy eight percent but fell by one percent in developed markets due to disposals during the quarter," said Haines.
Earnings from the group's Asia and Pacific businesses improved strongly to show a 23 million increase to 105 million in the second quarter.
($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
